old_value: {"id":"smallhold-z3ty.82","title":"WriteFreely update_post auth bypass: token_ok=false and auth.is_none() required","description":"writefreely_api.rs:107-118. The update_post auth logic has a gap. Line 108: token_ok is true when body.token matches article.edit_token. Line 111: if token_ok is false AND auth is None, return 401. Line 114-117: if body.token is provided but doesn't match, return 401. But if body.token is None and auth is Some(account), the request passes both checks — even if the authenticated user doesn't own the article. There's no ownership check: any authenticated user can update any article (as long as they don't provide a wrong token). new_value: {"description":"writefreely_api.rs:107-118 and 169-181. Both update_post and delete_post have the same auth bypass. The auth logic checks: (1) if token matches, pass; (2) if no token AND no auth, reject; (3) if token provided but wrong, reject. But if no token is provided and any authenticated user makes the request, it passes — there is no ownership check verifying the authenticated user owns the article. Any authenticated user can update or delete any WriteFreely article by omitting the token parameter."}
